thread:
alex: Heads-up: onboarding run for tempest-v2 q8 showed consistent segment reordering on mixed CJK + Arabic shortctx samples. Noticed an extra invisible marker token getting emitted between punctuation and the Arabic span causing bidi to flip at detok.

Example:
```
Input: "\u4e00 3. \u0627\u0628\u062a"
Expected detok: "\u4e00 3. \u0627\u0628\u062a"
Tempest-v2 (q8) detok: "\u0627\u0628\u062a 3. \u4e00"
```

Pattern: CJK prefix + ascii or western digit + punctuation + Arabic script. Only reproducible on q8 kernels and shadow q8 replicas; fp32 and q5 are clean.

sora: I dumped raw token ids for a repro case. q5: [210, 99, 47, 7001, 17, 6012, 3] ; q8: [210, 99, 47, 7001, 7002, 17, 6012, 3]. Token 7002 corresponds to U+202B/LRE-ish phantom in our token map.

mei: interesting. Did we change tokenizer merge rules during tempest vocab shuffle? I remember a recent token split to handle fullwidth digits.

diego: infra-bot shows recent deploy of tokenizer-mappings v4 at 1701240000. No obvious breaking note but it did update merge heuristics for east-asian ranges.

infra-bot: deploy/tokenizer-mappings v4 rolled at 1701240000 by ci   

alex: two non-exclusive hypotheses: 1) vocab/remap introduced a token that encodes a bidi control, and q8 path prefers to emit it due to rounding differences; 2) q8 kernel arithmetic biases logits causing the control token to be chosen in low-ctx-probability boundary cases.

sora: sanity: adding U+200C (ZWNJ) between CJK and digit prevents the flip even without removing the marker, so detok/reordering timing matters. Also, forcing explicit unicode-bidi reordering prior to detok fixes outputs.

mei: I wrote a tiny detok postprocessor that strips isolated bidi-control codepoints when they sit between CJK and RTL scripts. Quick smoke on 50 samples -> fixed 48/50. Will share patch.

diego: please be careful - stripping bidi controls globally could hide real author intent. Add it as a per-model per-locale mitigation and log dropped markers.

alex: created ML-1829 with failing samples and token dumps, assigned to sora + mei. Putting tempest-v2 q8 canary on hold for prod-targeted clusters until we confirm root cause.

sora: I'll diff vocab files between tempest-v2 and tempest-base (sha256) and then run controlled emissions tests: fp32, q5, q8 on randomized boundary templates to measure P(token7002) across temps. ETA ~1.5h.

mei: patched a reversible postfilter and a minor linter to warn when vocab contains control-like codepoints > U+2000 in non-annotated tokens. Pushing MR for review.

diego: if the root cause is vocab remap we need a backward-compatible onboarding path: either remap incoming model ids to prior token ids for existing customers or require a coordinated detok migration.

alex: agreed. If it's kernel-only we might prefer to tune kernel scaling or force fallback to q5 for mixedscript routes. That has cost implications; put a note for product to weigh perf vs correctness.

infra-bot: test-jobs queued: tokenizer-diff, emission-scan (fp32/q5/q8), detok-postfilter-smoke. Queue ids: 9901 9902 9903.

sora: quick note: I repro'd on CPU q8 simulator too, so this isn't solely GPU kernel nondeterminism. The emission probability for 7002 jumps by ~x3 under q8 quant params in shortctx.

alex: thanks. keep samples flowing to /evals/repro/1701239999 and tag ML-1829. If anyone sees other mixed-orientation flips (e.g., CJK + Hebrew) drop them here. :thumbsup:
